claim: A hearer’s lack of need to ask which arm helps explain the definite article.
evidence_summary: Constructed: Put it on an arm of your chair also needs no follow-up if either arm will do.
finding: The practical test alone cannot select the article. CGEL already recognizes nonunique and accommodated definites.
inference: Does the absence of a practical reason to ask which one suffice to predict use of the definite article?

evidence.passage: §6.1, p. 369. A hearer’s lack of need to ask which arm helps explain the definite article.
evidence.example: Give the same instruction with the arm of your chair and an arm of your chair when either arm will serve. In both cases the hearer can comply without asking which arm.
evidence.establishes: Lack of a practical need to ask cannot distinguish article choice here. CGEL separately allows accommodated referents and cases without a unique arm.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
